# Settings reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_docs.py from studioforge.settings_schema. Do not edit by hand. -->

Settings schema version **1** (`schema:` in `config.yaml`). 116 keys.

Settings live in `<data dir>/config.yaml`. The machine-readable form of this page is `GET /api/settings/schema` and `docs/contracts/settings-schema.json`.

**Environment overrides.** Every key can also be given as an environment variable: `SF_` plus the dotted key in upper case with `.` written as `__` (`server.port` is `SF_SERVER__PORT`). Environment values are first-run defaults: once `config.yaml` names a key, the file wins. Only `SF_DATA_DIR` and `SF_CONFIG` are authoritative at all times.

**Levels.** *Basic* keys are the ones most installs touch; everything else is *Advanced*. **Restart** means a change does not take effect on a running server.

| `schema` | `int` | `1` | >= 1 | advanced | no | `SF_SCHEMA_VERSION` | Layout version of config.yaml. Older files without it load as version 1. |

| Key | Type | Default | Valid values | Level | Restart | Env | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `models.dir` | `path \| null` | `null` | - | basic | no | `SF_MODELS__DIR` | Your GGUF library. Left null, first run probes for an LM Studio one (including the relocated `downloadsFolder` in ~/.lmstudio/settings.json). models.extra_dirs adds more, scanned after it. |
| `models.extra_dirs` | `list[path]` | `[]` | - | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__EXTRA_DIRS` | Further directories scanned for models, after models.dir. |
| `models.default_ctx` | `int` | `8192` | > 0 | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__DEFAULT_CTX` | The context FLOOR. The planner never recommends less than this to buy an extra parallel slot. |
| `models.default_ttl_s` | `int` | `600` | >= 0 | basic | no | `SF_MODELS__DEFAULT_TTL_S` | Idle countdown for a load that names no tier and has no per-tier entry: 10 minutes since the last request against it. A load with no priority is a background load (D46), and a background model nobody has asked for in ten minutes is VRAM somebody else could use. 0 = never unload. |
| `models.ttl_by_priority` | `map[int, int]` | `{"1":900,"2":900,"3":600}` | - | basic | no | `SF_MODELS__TTL_BY_PRIORITY` | Idle TTL per load tier since the last request: {1: 900, 2: 900, 3: 600} -- the chat model and an agent's model idle out after 15 minutes, background (and any load that named no tier) after 10. Empty = default_ttl_s for every tier. |
| `models.auto_unload_idle_s` | `int \| null` | `null` | > 0 | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__AUTO_UNLOAD_IDLE_S` | Null = off. Seconds: every model with no per-model ttl_s and no pin unloads after that much idle time, whatever its tier (replaces the two timers above); a request's own ttl still wins (D75). |
| `models.default_kv_cache_type` | `"auto" \| "f32" \| "f16" \| "bf16" \| "q8_0" \| "q5_1" \| "q5_0" \| "q4_1" \| "q4_0"` | `auto` | one of `auto`, `f32`, `f16`, `bf16`, `q8_0`, `q5_1`, `q5_0`, `q4_1`, `q4_0` | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__DEFAULT_KV_CACHE_TYPE` | "auto": the planner picks per model rather than forcing one type on the whole library. |
| `models.default_parallel` | `int \| "auto"` | `auto` | one of `auto` | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__DEFAULT_PARALLEL` | "auto": the planner sizes the slot count per model and per placement (see DECISIONS.md D17) instead of forcing every load to one conversation. |
| `models.ctx_per_slot_default` | `int` | `32768` | > 0 | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__CTX_PER_SLOT_DEFAULT` | Per-slot context the parallel estimator assumes when nothing else says. Only used to *size* the slot count and to build the catalog's loading-options table; it never overrides a planned or explicit ctx_size. |
| `models.default_flash_attn` | `"on" \| "off" \| "auto"` | `on` | one of `on`, `off`, `auto` | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__DEFAULT_FLASH_ATTN` | "on" rather than "auto": flash attention is a large KV-bandwidth and memory win and is supported on every GPU from Ampere (sm_80) up, which is all of this rig. "auto" defers the same decision to the engine and has been observed to decline it. |
| `models.default_cache_reuse` | `int` | `256` | >= 0 | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__DEFAULT_CACHE_REUSE` | Prompt-cache reuse: the OpenClaw latency win |
| `models.auto_ctx_checkpoints` | `int \| null` | `8` | >= 0 | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__AUTO_CTX_CHECKPOINTS` | Context checkpoints for models whose cache cannot be rolled back (sliding-window "iswa" and hybrid ones; full-attention models never make them). Each checkpoint copies the slot's sliding-window cells into HOST RAM (~800 MiB at f16 for a 31B Gemma-4), so the count is capped below the engine's 32. A model's own ctx_checkpoints / checkpoint_min_step setting wins. null = pass nothing (the engine's defaults: 32, 8192 tokens apart). |
| `models.auto_checkpoint_min_step` | `int \| null` | `null` | >= 0 | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__AUTO_CHECKPOINT_MIN_STEP` | `--checkpoint-min-step` for the same models (D72). `None` -- the shipped value -- passes nothing and keeps the engine's 8192: the last user message and the end of every prompt are checkpointed whatever the spacing, which is where a chat's next turn diverges, so a denser spacing... |
| `models.default_reasoning_format` | `"none" \| "deepseek" \| "deepseek-legacy"` | `none` | one of `none`, `deepseek`, `deepseek-legacy` | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__DEFAULT_REASONING_FORMAT` | "none" keeps a reasoning model's thoughts inline in message.content. llama.cpp's default ("auto") splits them into reasoning_content and leaves content empty, which reads as an empty reply to every OpenAI client. |
| `models.thinking_default_ctx` | `int` | `32768` | > 0 | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__THINKING_DEFAULT_CTX` | Reasoning models spend their budget thinking before answering, so the ordinary default truncates the chain of thought AND the visible answer. Applied only when a thinking model has no explicit ctx_size, clamped to the model's trained window and to what actually fits. |
| `models.target_ctx` | `int` | `1048576` | > 0 | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__TARGET_CTX` | What every load AIMS for, halving down to what actually fits in VRAM, never below default_ctx. |
| `models.auto_load_pinned` | `bool` | `true` | - | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__AUTO_LOAD_PINNED` | Pinned models are loaded at startup AND kept resident: the reconciler reloads one that goes down -- crash past max_restarts, a failure, a pin set while unloaded -- unless a caller explicitly unloaded it (D41). Turning this off reduces a pin to "no idle TTL, never evicted". |
| `models.default_model` | `string \| null` | `null` | - | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__DEFAULT_MODEL` | Served when a request omits "model", or names one of DEFAULT_MODEL_ALIASES ("local-model", "default", "auto"). LM Studio clients send "local-model" as a fallback, so 404-ing it breaks them for no good reason. |
| `models.preload_default_model` | `bool` | `false` | - | advanced | no | `SF_MODELS__PRELOAD_DEFAULT_MODEL` | Load the default model at startup so the first request is not also the first (slow) load. |

| Key | Type | Default | Valid values | Level | Restart | Env | Description |

| `engine.cuda_variant` | `string` | `auto` | - | advanced | yes | `SF_ENGINE__CUDA_VARIANT` | "auto" picks the CUDA build matching your driver; pin it ("13.3", "12.4") if the guess is wrong. |
| `engine.keep_versions` | `int` | `3` | > 0 | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__KEEP_VERSIONS` | Installed engine builds to keep; older ones are pruned. |
| `engine.allow_source_build` | `bool` | `true` | - | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__ALLOW_SOURCE_BUILD` | Build llama.cpp from source when no prebuilt asset fits. |
| `engine.repo` | `string` | `ggml-org/llama.cpp` | - | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__REPO` | GitHub repository engine builds are downloaded from. |
| `engine.update_channel` | `"stable" \| "latest"` | `stable` | one of `stable`, `latest` | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__UPDATE_CHANNEL` | Which release "Check for update" and `engine --update` act on (D62). "stable": the bNNNN build named by upstream's newest vX.Y.Z version release (its nightly-tag.txt asset); "latest": the newest bNNNN build with an asset this box can install. The other channel is still reported. |
| `engine.smoke_test_timeout_s` | `float` | `180.0` | > 0 | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__SMOKE_TEST_TIMEOUT_S` | Seconds a new engine build gets to pass its smoke test. |
| `engine.cache_ram_mb` | `int \| "auto"` | `auto` | one of `auto` | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__CACHE_RAM_MB` | Host-RAM prompt cache (`--cache-ram`): evicted prompt prefixes are kept in system memory instead of recomputed. Costs no VRAM, changes no output, so it is on by default. "auto" = a POOL of 25% of RAM capped at 32 GiB, shared out among the loaded models; an explicit integer is per model, verbatim. 0 disables it, -1 is the engine's "no limit". |
| `engine.ubatch_size` | `int \| null` | `null` | > 0 | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__UBATCH_SIZE` | `--ubatch-size` for every model that does not set its own. Raising it buys prompt speed with compute-buffer VRAM the planner then charges per card (D40) -- a trade to make knowingly, so it ships unset (engine's 512). |
| `engine.ubatch_many_slots` | `int \| null` | `1024` | > 0 | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__UBATCH_MANY_SLOTS` | `--ubatch-size` for a MANY-SLOT launch (>4 slots) when nothing above is set. D38 measured a larger micro-batch as pure prefill speed and D40 made the estimate charge its VRAM, so the automatic raise is safe (error direction: a refused context, never an OOM). Helps exactly the heavy concurrent prefill; a single-stream load stays at the engine's 512. null turns the automatic raise off. |
| `engine.backend_sampling` | `bool` | `false` | - | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__BACKEND_SAMPLING` | `--backend-sampling`: GPU-side sampling. b10425 marks it EXPERIMENTAL, so it is off under the quality-first rule (only lossless, non-experimental features ship enabled). |
| `engine.strict_gpu` | `bool` | `true` | - | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__STRICT_GPU` | STRICT_GPU: every load is fully resident on the GPU (`-ngl 999 --fit off` are always passed; --cpu-moe / --n-cpu-moe / --no-kv-offload and the other CPU-offload flags are refused). false only makes a model's own, off-by- default `allow_partial_cpu_offload` setting effective -- see docs/ENGINES.md. |
| `engine.preference` | `"balanced" \| "fastest_replies" \| "fastest_long_prompts"` | `balanced` | one of `balanced`, `fastest_replies`, `fastest_long_prompts` | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__PREFERENCE` | Which backend to favour when several are benchmarked for a GPU: balanced, fastest_replies (token generation) or fastest_long_prompts (prompt processing). Nothing benchmarks on its own; see docs/ENGINES.md. |
| `engine.require_verified` | `bool` | `false` | - | advanced | no | `SF_ENGINE__REQUIRE_VERIFIED` | True = refuse to install an engine archive that has no published SHA-256. false (default) installs it, records verified: false and warns. |

| `gpu.probe_cache_s` | `float` | `2.0` | >= 0 | advanced | yes | `SF_GPU__PROBE_CACHE_S` | Seconds a ROCm / Vulkan / Metal probe result is reused before the vendor tool (`amd-smi`, `vulkaninfo`, `system_profiler`) runs again. Past it the call returns the last good answer (or "no GPUs" if there is none) and the tool keeps running in the background, so a hung tool cannot stall a request. Restart required. |

## tenants

| Key | Type | Default | Valid values | Level | Restart | Env | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tenants.registry` | `list[TenantEntry]` | `[]` | - | advanced | yes | `SF_TENANTS__REGISTRY` | The tenant registry (D77, docs/TENANTS.md): other programs that share these GPUs. Declaring one here puts it on the Tenants card with live health before it has registered itself; a program may also announce itself at runtime with POST /api/tenants/register (the two merge by name). StudioForge never starts or stops a tenant (D79): `kind: module` only means it may be ASKED to warm through its own warm_url. Every URL must be loopback, a tailnet address (100.64.0.0/10) or a host in allowed_hosts below; nothing else is ever called, and names are never resolved. Two examples, commented out: registry: # SpeechForge, a speech module on the same box: one card, class 2. - name: speechforge kind: module health_url: http://127.0.0.1:1236/health warm_url: http://127.0.0.1:1236/v1/speech/warm default_priority: 2 notes: speech-to-text and text-to-speech; leases one card while a session is open # ClawForge2, the image gateway: a plain tenant that leases ComfyUI's card. - name: clawforge2 kind: tenant health_url: http://127.0.0.1:8700/health status_url: http://127.0.0.1:8700/ui/api/status default_priority: 3 |
| `tenants.health_interval_s` | `float` | `30.0` | > 0 | advanced | yes | `SF_TENANTS__HEALTH_INTERVAL_S` | How often every registered `health_url` is polled. |
| `tenants.health_timeout_s` | `float` | `2.0` | > 0 | advanced | yes | `SF_TENANTS__HEALTH_TIMEOUT_S` | Per-poll HTTP timeout. Two seconds: a health route that takes longer is unhealthy for this purpose, and the poller must never pile up. |
| `tenants.allowed_hosts` | `list[string]` | `[]` | - | advanced | yes | `SF_TENANTS__ALLOWED_HOSTS` | Hosts, beyond loopback and the tailnet range, a tenant URL may name -- as IP literals or as names compared verbatim (never resolved). |
